options.hook: Epic Games used AI to convert more than 20,000 of Fortnite's Blueprints into about 3 million lines of Verse, and on that basis Unreal Engine 6 will ship without Blueprints.
options.story: In an update reported on 20 November 2026, Epic Games said an AI-assisted run converted more than 20,000 of Fortnite's visual Blueprints into a working prototype in its Verse language, about 3 million lines, a job it had expected to take years. On that basis Unreal Engine 6, the engine game studios build on, will ship without Blueprints.

options.hook: Maxon, the software company behind Cinema 4D and ZBrush, now sells AI model generation inside its apps, run on other firms' models such as Tripo and Rodin and billed in credits.
options.story: Maxon, which makes Cinema 4D and ZBrush, the 3D software that 3D studios and artists use, launched Maxon Plus in November 2026, a cloud subscription whose Model Generator turns a prompt, photo or sketch into an editable 3D model. The work runs on third-party AI providers such as Tripo and Rodin, and is sold in credits.

options.hook: Google's Genie 4 streams a playable 720p world at 24 frames a second to game developers, at roughly $0.10 a second, for up to 120 seconds a session.
options.story: On 19 November 2026 Google made Genie 4 available to game developers through the Gemini API and AI Studio. It generates a continuous 720p world at 24 frames a second with sound, steered live with the keyboard and text prompts, and each frame is generated as the session runs. PPC Land reports a price of roughly $0.10 per second, sessions of up to 120 seconds, and that visual stability may degrade after 60 to 90 seconds.

options.hook: iZotope's Nectar 5 transcribes a sung vocal into lyrics in the edit window, so a producer selects a single word and adds up to seven effects to it.
options.story: iZotope released Nectar 5, its vocal plugin for music producers, on 24 November 2026 at an introductory $179 until 7 December, then $249. Its Moments module transcribes the sung lyrics in the edit window, so a producer selects a word or phrase and adds up to seven effects to it, and its Vocal Assistant listens to part of the vocal and designs a processing chain.

options.hook: Manchester Animation Festival will bar generative AI films from 2027, as Ottawa's festival says entrants are lying on their forms, and festivals decide which animated films win distribution deals.
options.story: Manchester Animation Festival announced that from 2027 a film is ineligible if a generative model creates or alters any part of its final moving image. Speaking to Cartoon Brew on 20 November 2026, Ottawa's artistic director said some animators are lying on their forms, marking AI films as 3D.

options.hook: A Binding of Isaac update shipped Suno-made music with no AI label on Steam, and players found Suno's tag inside the music files' metadata.
options.story: On 19 November 2026 Nicalis added a themed daily run to the video game The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ on Steam; the next day a Reddit user showed its music files carried Suno metadata. The game's Steam page had no AI disclosure, recent reviews fell to 8% positive, and Nicalis removed the generated music.

options.hook: HeyGen says its new Avatar 6 is 84.4% indistinguishable from real video, and its own research page shows raters picked it as the real clip 42.2% of the time.
options.story: HeyGen released Avatar 6 on 17 November 2026, a model that turns a photo or a short clip plus an audio track into a talking video for creators. Its research page explains its headline: shown real footage and Avatar 6 side by side, raters picked Avatar 6 as the real one 42.2% of the time across 270 answers, which HeyGen scores as 84.4% of the way to a coin toss. Shown one clip at a time, 65.1% of Avatar 6 clips were judged real against 78.9% of real recordings.

options.hook: Tor pulled the cover of Ilona Andrews's new novel after learning generative AI was used to make it, though the authors' contract and Tor's art contracts both forbid it.
options.story: On 20 November 2026 Tor Publishing Group withdrew the newly revealed cover of Ilona Andrews's fantasy novel This Crown Will Not Rule Me after learning generative AI had been used to make it, without the knowledge of Tor or the authors. The authors' contract and Tor's contracts with cover artists both prohibit generative AI. Readers raised it after the reveal, and Tor said it takes full responsibility for the breakdown in its review process.

What I don't know: TikTok's actual moderation capacity or intent behind the design, the sources establish the mechanism, not the motive. Hook: "Starbucks spends about $400 million a year on software, and it's building AI tools that could replace some of it." recent_posts.words: Will your AI auditor find your missing money, or the skeletons in your closet? Every new instrument has overturned things people were sure of, and AI with a strict checker beside it has started doing the same to maths: the facts your business repeats most are the ones most worth re-checking. Headline: AI's first big job may be finding what we got wrong. Hook: "For 40 years, a step in one of the biggest proofs in maths did not hold, and nobody noticed." The chain: the microscope, DNA testing and now AI each found errors in what experts had signed off; Axiom's agents rewrote 15,000 pages so a computer could check every step, and found 34 departures from the record, one a real gap in a 1986 proof; the theorem still stands. What's actually going on: AI is a poor judge on its own and a superb auditor with a checker beside it. Where we land: the next thing to be re-checked may be something you were taught as fact. recent_posts.title: Where does AI get built when towns say no?
recent_posts.words: Where does AI get built when towns say no? The midterms turned AI into a vote about the electricity bill. Whether AI gets built in America, and how fast and how cheaply, is now being decided by voters and local councils; Washington and the tech companies no longer get the last word. So the builders are looking for ways round, and those ways round will change what AI looks like and where it lives. In Krish's words, the piece is "about the future of AI after the midterms", and he would "rather not make predictions about politics". America has a new least-wanted neighbour. In a Gallup poll this spring, 71% of Americans said they did not want an AI data centre built near them; only 53% said the same about a nuclear power plant. Then on 3 November, towns in 10 states held 41 votes on data centres, 21 of them in Ohio, and 40 went against the data centre. Within days OpenAI promised, again, to pay the full cost of powering its own data centres: a promise it first made in January.
